title: Lior and the Confession
premise: Estate lawyer Tamsin Sterling is hired by a dying woman, Lior Vance, who pays a fortune in advance for one impossible task: prove that her own murder — predicted in a will dated three days after her expected death — will not happen. As Tamsin investigates the family gathered at the Vance estate, he discovers the will's author knows details of the case file that don't yet exist, suggesting either a brilliant fraud or someone manipulating events toward a scripted death. The killer is Lior's adopted son, who forged the will to establish an insanity defense in advance, and Tamsin must expose him before the prophecy fulfills itself; in the end, Lior survives by publicly disinheriting everyone, choosing a found family over blood, while Tamsin confronts his own inherited name and what belonging truly costs.
about_author: August Sterling is the pen name of a former probate clerk who spent a decade reading other people's final wishes before turning to fiction. They write mysteries about paper trails, family secrets, and the strange legal machinery of death.

chapters.title: The Will That Shouldn't Exist
chapters.summary: Tamsin Sterling, a meticulous estate lawyer, receives a retainer from Lior Vance: a notarized will dated for a death that hasn't occurred, bequeathing her estate contingent on proving she won't be murdered. Through Tamsin's POV, we feel his professional unease curdle into fascination. Emotional beat: intrigue laced with dread as the impossible document lands on his desk.

chapters.title: Advance Payment
chapters.summary: Lior, sharp-tongued and terminally ill, explains the terms in her sunlit study: if Tamsin can demonstrate no murder will occur within thirty days, he keeps the fee; if she dies violently, he must unmask the killer using only the will's clues. Tamsin's POV establishes their wary rapport. Emotional beat: reluctant commitment — he takes the case against every instinct.

chapters.title: House of Vances
chapters.summary: Tamsin arrives at Blackthorn Grange, where the family has assembled for Lior's 'last summer': son Marcus, daughter-in-law Priya, estranged brother Aldous, and caretaker Nell. His POV catalogs each suspect's alibi-shaped behavior. Emotional beat: claustrophobic unease — a house already rehearsing its grief.

chapters.title: Details Before the Fact
chapters.summary: Tamsin cross-references the will's language against the local police's cold-case files and finds phrases matching evidence descriptions that shouldn't exist yet — a broken stair rail, a spilled decanter. His POV shifts between lawyerly rigor and creeping fear. Emotional beat: the first true chill of the uncanny.

chapters.title: Marcus's Inheritance
chapters.summary: Marcus, the adopted heir, gives Tamsin a polished interview but flinches at questions about the will's date. A brief interlude from Marcus's POV reveals his resentment of being 'chosen' rather than born. Emotional beat: sympathy shading into suspicion — the reader sees his wound before seeing his guilt.

chapters.title: Aldous's Ledger
chapters.summary: Uncle Aldous, drowning in debts, shows Tamsin old family ledgers revealing the Vance fortune came from a falsified patent decades ago. Tamsin realizes inheritance in this family has always been theft. Emotional beat: moral vertigo — everyone here is guilty of something.

chapters.title: Nell Knows the Stairs
chapters.summary: Caretaker Nell mentions the stair rail was repaired last month — before the will described it breaking. Tamsin begins to suspect the will isn't predicting a murder but scheduling one. His POV tightens with urgency. Emotional beat: the pivot from mystery to countdown.

chapters.title: The Forger's Hand
chapters.summary: A graphologist friend confirms the will's signature is genuine but the drafting style matches documents Marcus filed years ago. Tamsin confronts the possibility that Marcus wrote his mother's death into law. Emotional beat: cold clarity — the trap has an author.

chapters.title: Priya's Silence
chapters.summary: Priya privately tells Tamsin she found draft pages of the will in Marcus's study weeks ago and said nothing, terrified of what it implied. Her POV chapter exposes her complicity through fear. Emotional beat: guilt and the terrible weight of knowing too late.

chapters.title: Storm Warning
chapters.summary: A storm seals the roads on the night the will's timeline points to. Tamsin begs Lior to leave; she refuses, insisting the game must play out to catch the killer cleanly. His POV wrestles with protecting a client determined to be bait. Emotional beat: dread rising like floodwater.

chapters.title: The Broken Rail
chapters.summary: The stair rail snaps under Lior's hand — but Nell, forewarned by Tamsin, catches her. Someone sabotaged it exactly as the will described. Tamsin's POV races through the house finding everyone accounted for except one vanished hour. Emotional beat: terror narrowly averted, certainty hardening.

chapters.title: Case File Ghost
chapters.summary: Police arrive and find their own investigative notes mirrored in the will's phrasing — meaning someone inside the investigation leaked, or the will was written by someone who plans to control the record itself. Tamsin's POV spirals. Emotional beat: paranoia — the killer is editing reality.

chapters.title: What Adoption Owes
chapters.summary: Lior confesses to Tamsin why she adopted Marcus: to replace a child she lost, and how her love became a debt he could never repay. Her POV chapter humanizes both victim and suspect. Emotional beat: heartbreak — inheritance as an unpaid emotional bill.

chapters.title: The Second Document
chapters.summary: Tamsin discovers a companion document: a psychiatric evaluation, pre-dated, establishing Marcus's temporary insanity — the perfect defense, prepared before any crime. His POV lays out the full legal architecture of the plot. Emotional beat: grim admiration for the killer's cunning.

chapters.title: Confrontation in the Greenhouse
chapters.summary: Tamsin corners Marcus, who neither denies nor confesses, arguing that a life spent as someone's 'proof of love' justifies reclaiming authorship of his own story. Dual tension in Tamsin's POV. Emotional beat: the theme made flesh — identity versus inheritance.

chapters.title: Nell's Testimony
chapters.summary: Nell admits Marcus paid her to alter the rail's maintenance records, believing it harmless paperwork. Her testimony completes the chain of evidence. Brief Nell POV shows a loyal servant's shattered trust. Emotional beat: sorrowful confirmation — the conspiracy unravels.

chapters.title: The Last Clause
chapters.summary: Re-reading the will, Tamsin finds a hidden clause: if Lior dies before the thirty days, the estate passes to whoever proves the will fraudulent — a trap Marcus built for himself, or perhaps for Tamsin. His POV races to decode intent. Emotional beat: the floor drops out.

chapters.title: Night of the Will
chapters.summary: On the will's named date, the power fails and Marcus comes for Lior with the staged scene half-built. Tamsin intervenes; a struggle in the dark library ends with Marcus restrained as dawn breaks. Climactic action in Tamsin's POV. Emotional beat: white-knuckle climax — the prophecy refused.

chapters.title: Confession
chapters.summary: Marcus confesses in full: the forged will, the planted evidence, the engineered insanity plea — all to convert a lifetime of being chosen into a verdict of being broken. His raw confession chapter closes his arc. Emotional beat: devastating catharsis and pity without absolution.

chapters.title: Disinheritance
chapters.summary: Lior executes a new will leaving nearly everything to a foundation for foster youth, keeping only enough to live simply, and asks Tamsin to witness it. His POV frames the act as her real victory. Emotional beat: quiet triumph — severing the poisoned line of inheritance.

chapters.title: Sterling's Own Name
chapters.summary: In the aftermath, Tamsin researches his own inherited name and the father he never knew, realizing he too has been living inside a document written before his birth. Reflective first-person close. Emotional beat: personal reckoning mirroring the case.

chapters.title: Belonging
chapters.summary: Months later, Tamsin visits Lior at her small cottage by the sea, where Nell cooks dinner and Priya writes letters to Marcus in prison. The found family holds. Final chapter resolves the themes: identity is chosen daily, not inherited once. Emotional beat: warm, earned peace.
